thread:
Samir: Heads-up — noticed a perf/regression on chat workloads after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. p95 generation latency up ~18% on long-context sessions.
Maya: interesting, which workloads? RAG or normal chat?
Samir: primarily chat w/ long convo prefixes and structured JSON outputs. RAG seems less impacted.  Weights: p50 ~ 120ms -> 135ms, p95 ~ 420ms -> 495ms. KV cache hit-rate dropped for these sessions.
Josh: any change to cache keying code in that change? I thought kernel selector shouldn't touch prefix hashing.
Samir: it was a subtle change — we started merging adjacent prefix fragments early ("context shingling") to improve kernel packing. That changed the prefix fingerprint ordering so many keys no longer match the cached entries.
Lee: ah, so collision-free keys became "reordered" keys. Do you have hit numbers?
Samir: before: chat-prefix hit-rate ~72% (sampled over 24h). after: ~45% for the same traffic slice. RAG hit-rate ~70->68 (negligible). Completions mostly unaffected.
Maya: that explains latency spike — more cold KV lookups + extra token work on session warmup. Any easy rollback?
Samir: I've got a diagnostic branch to revert the shingling reorder. If we revert, hit-rate returns to ~70% in local replay. But curious if we can keep packing gains without harming key stability.
Josh: can we make shingling deterministic w.r.t. original prefix boundaries? e.g., use stable canonicalization that includes fragment indices in the fingerprint.
Samir: tried adding fragment index to fingerprint; hit-rate improved to ~68% but kernel packing benefits drop ~10%. It's a tradeoff.
Anya: Also seeing batching heuristics amplify the regression. Batcher coalesces based on cache locality; with lower hit-rate, we get smaller batches and kernel swap frequency increases. p95 compounding there.
Lee: we should profile kernel-switch frequency per minute. Any telemetry?
Samir: yes — attached sample trace from canary node:
```
2026-03-15T14:03:11Z node=canary-7 kernel_swap=12/min batch_size_avg=6 kv_hit_rate=0.46
2026-03-15T14:04:11Z node=canary-7 kernel_swap=15/min batch_size_avg=5 kv_hit_rate=0.44
```
Josh: thanks. Also check KV cache key cardinality — shingling might explode key space for long context.
Maya: I ran a quick quant: distinct prefix keys per session went from median 4 -> 9 for long conversations after the change. That likely increases eviction churn.
Anya: eviction + smaller batches = more memory pressure and kernel thrash. Not good.
Samir: Proposed short-term mitigation: 1) rollback reorder change and redeploy to canary; 2) add probe that pins fragment ordering (opt-in) for 24h to collect A/B; 3) improve key canonicalizer to include session-level stable id to coalesce where safe.
Lee: agree rollback to stop immediate regression. We should also add a metric for "prefix_key_turnover" (unique keys/sec per session) so we can detect this class of regressions earlier.
Maya: can you post the revert PR? I'll run replay against the top-10 chat traces and attach perf diffs.
Samir: PR: https://git.redwood.internal/r/infer/runtime/+/8347 — includes revert + test harness. @infra-bot can you trigger a canary deploy?
infra-bot: deploy request received for ref 8347. Starting canary in eng-runtime-prod-canary.
Josh: for medium-term: consider shingling with locality-preserving hashing (e.g., rolling-window hashed but anchored to absolute token offsets) so we don't rekey on minor fragment merges.
Anya: also add a batcher hook that signals when kv_hit_rate < 0.6 so it can switch to latency-optimized scheduling (bigger join windows) to avoid micro-batching thrash.
Samir: good idea — that'll at least reduce amplification while we iterate on keying.
Maya: replay results: revert returned kv_hit_rate from 0.45 -> 0.71 and p95 back to baseline within the canary traffic slice. attaching short CSV in follow-up.
Lee: plan: revert full rollout, instrument prefix_key_turnover, add canary A/B for the new canonicalizer variant, and add batcher fallback if kv_hit_rate drops.
Samir: I'll merge revert and kick off full canary. Follow-ups: let's own a small tech spec for deterministic shingling and batching heuristics to avoid reintroducing this.
Maya: +1, will start doc draft.
Josh: thanks all. Small ask — add a label to PRs that touch any cache key logic so we can trigger extra replay tests automatically.
Anya: putting that in backlog.
Samir: deploying now. infra-bot will post results.
infra-bot: canary deploy 8347 succeeded (3/3 canaries healthy). Monitoring kv_hit_rate & p95.
Samir: initial post-deploy numbers looking good — kv_hit_rate ~0.70, p95 back to baseline. Closing thread but keeping follow-ups on #eng-runtime to track spec.
